facts.statement: Corythosaurus is a genus of dinosaur.
facts.quote: taxon: Corythosaurus

facts.statement: Corythosaurus was described by Barnum Brown in 1914.
facts.quote: authority: Brown, 1914

facts.statement: Corythosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous epoch, specifically the Campanian age.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous (Campanian)

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Corythosaurus is Corythosaurus casuarius.
facts.quote: type_species: Corythosaurus casuarius

facts.statement: Other species once assigned to Corythosaurus include C. intermedius, originally named Stephanosaurus, and C. stebingeri, originally named H. stebingeri.

facts.statement: Corythosaurus is classified as a lambeosaurine, a subgroup of hadrosaurid dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Corythosaurus is now thought to be a lambeosaurine

facts.statement: Corythosaurus had an estimated length of 7.7 to 9 meters and a skull with a crest that was 70.8 centimeters tall.
facts.quote: Corythosaurus has an estimated length of 7.7 - 9 m and has a skull, including the crest, that is 70.8 cm tall

facts.statement: The estimated length of Corythosaurus ranges from 7.7 to 9 meters.
facts.quote: Corythosaurus has an estimated length of 7.7 - 9 m

facts.statement: A preserved specimen contained conifer needles, seeds, twigs, and fruits, suggesting Corythosaurus fed on these plant materials.
facts.quote: One Corythosaurus specimen has even been preserved with its last meal in its chest cavity. Inside the cavity were remains of conifer needles, seeds, twigs, and fruits, suggesting that Corythosaurus probably fed on all of these

facts.statement: The first Corythosaurus specimen, AMNH 5240, was discovered in 1911 by Barnum Brown in the Red Deer River of Alberta.
facts.quote: The first specimen, AMNH 5240, was discovered in 1911 by Barnum Brown in Red Deer River of Alberta

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Corythosaurus was found in the Belly River Group.
facts.quote: The specimen came from the Belly River Group of the province

facts.statement: Barnum Brown named the type species Corythosaurus casuarius in 1914 based on a specimen he collected in 1912.
facts.quote: The type species, Corythosaurus casuarius, was named by Barnum Brown in 1914, based on the first specimen collected by him in 1912

facts.statement: Two well-preserved Corythosaurus specimens found by Charles H. Sternberg in 1912 were lost in 1916 when the ship SS Mount Temple was sunk during World War I.
facts.quote: The two best preserved specimens of Corythosaurus, found by Charles H. Sternberg in 1912, were lost on December 6, 1916, while being carried by the SS Mount Temple to the United Kingdom during World War I

facts.statement: Corythosaurus intermedius lived slightly later in the Campanian stage than Corythosaurus casuarius.
facts.quote: C. intermedius lived at a slightly later time in the Campanian than C. casuarius

facts.statement: Research suggests that differences in skull size and shape among Corythosaurus species may be related to sex and age rather than distinct species.
facts.quote: He found that the differences in size and shape may have actually been related to the sex and age of the animal

facts.statement: The name Corythosaurus means "helmeted lizard" and is derived from the Greek word for a Corinthian helmet.
facts.quote: The generic name Corythosaurus is derived from the Greek κόρυθος,(korythos), "Corinthian helmet", and means "helmeted lizard"

facts.statement: Specimen AMNH 5338 was found in 1914 by Barnum Brown and Peter Kaisen.
facts.quote: Another specimen, AMNH 5338, was found in 1914 by Brown and Peter Kaisen

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton was articulated and missing only the last 0.61 meters of the tail and the front legs.
facts.quote: The skeleton was articulated and missing only about the last 0.61 m of the tail and front legs

facts.statement: The discovery of the holotype was notable for preserving impressions of much of the creature's skin.
facts.quote: As well as an almost complete skeleton, the find was notable because impressions of much of the creature's skin had also survived

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the crest functioned like a trombone to amplify sound waves produced by exhalation.
facts.quote: As in a trombone, sound waves would travel through many chambers in the crest and then get amplified when Corythosaurus exhaled

facts.statement: Benson et al. (2012) estimated the average length of Corythosaurus to be 9 meters.
facts.quote: Benson et al. (2012) estimated that Corythosaurus has an average length of 9 m

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul (2016) estimated C. casuarius reached 8 meters and 2.8 tonnes, while C. intermedius reached 7.7 meters and 2.5 tonnes.
facts.quote: In 2016, Gregory S. Paul estimated that C. casuarius reached 8 m long and 2.8 MT in weight and that C. intermedius reached 7.7 m in length and 2.5 MT in weight

facts.statement: The most likely function of the Corythosaurus crest is thought to be vocalization.
facts.quote: The most likely function of the crest is thought to be vocalization

facts.statement: More than twenty skulls of Corythosaurus have been discovered.
facts.quote: Over twenty skulls have been found from this dinosaur.

facts.statement: Corythosaurus possessed a tall, elaborate bony crest on its skull containing elongated nasal passages.
facts.quote: As with other lambeosaurines, the animal bore a tall, elaborate, bony crest atop its skull that contained the elongate narial passages.

facts.statement: The crest of Corythosaurus resembles that of a cassowary or a Corinthian helmet.
facts.quote: The crests of Corythosaurus resemble that of a cassowary or a Corinthian helmet.

facts.statement: The crest of the type specimen of Corythosaurus measured 83.7 cm in length from beak to tip, 81.2 cm in total length, and 70.8 cm in height.
facts.quote: The total length of the crest from the beak to the uppermost tip of the type specimen is 83.7 cm, its total length is 81.2 cm, and its height is 70.8 cm.

facts.statement: The lower jaw of the holotype of Corythosaurus was 66.9 cm long and 10 cm deep.
facts.quote: The lower jaw of the holotype is 66.9 cm long and 10 cm deep.

facts.statement: The sides and tail of the Corythosaurus holotype were covered in various types of scales.
facts.quote: In the holotype of C. casuarius, the sides and tail are covered in scales of several types.

facts.statement: Research later revealed that the "webs" on Corythosaurus were actually deflated padding similar to that found in modern mammals.
facts.quote: However, it was later discovered that the so-called "webs" were in fact deflated padding, much like that found on many modern mammals.

facts.statement: Barnum Brown identified a set of distinguishing characters for Corythosaurus in 1914.
facts.quote: A set of characters were indicated by Barnum Brown in 1914 to distinguish Corythosaurus from all other hadrosaurids from Alberta.

facts.statement: Barnum Brown expanded the list of distinguishing features for Corythosaurus in 1916.
facts.quote: In 1916, Brown expanded the character set to include even more features.

facts.statement: Ossified tendons were present on all vertebrae of Corythosaurus except those in the neck region.
facts.quote: Ossified tendons are present on all the vertebrae, except for those in the cervical region.

facts.statement: It is debated regarding the anatomy of the crest, as Barnum Brown incorrectly identified the praemaxillae as nasals, leading to errors about their extent and separation.
facts.quote: Brown assumed that they extended from the beaks' tip to the highest spot along the crest and that, unlike those in other genera, the nasals meet in the center and are not separated in front by an ascending premaxillary process. However, Brown mistook the praemaxillae for the nasals.

facts.statement: Many presumed traits of the Corythosaurus snout described by Brown are incorrect due to his confusion between the praemaxillae, nasal bones, and frontals.
facts.quote: Again, the presumed traits of the snout are incorrect because Brown confused the praemaxillae with the nasal bones and the nasal bones with the frontals.

facts.statement: Many postcranial traits once thought unique to Corythosaurus are now known to be shared with other lambeosaurines.
facts.quote: Most of the postcranial traits are today known to be shared with various other lambeosaurines.

facts.statement: Corythosaurus is classified as a hadrosaurid dinosaur in the subfamily Lambeosaurinae.
facts.quote: Corythosaurus is currently classified as a hadrosaurid in the subfamily Lambeosaurinae.

facts.statement: Research by Benson et al. (2012) suggests Corythosaurus is closely related to Velafrons, Nipponosaurus, and Hypacrosaurus, forming a group of fan-crested lambeosaurines.
facts.quote: Benson et al. (2012) found that Corythosaurus was closely related to Velafrons, Nipponosaurus, and Hypacrosaurus, with them forming a group of fan-crested lambeosaurines.

facts.statement: Based on Late Cretaceous climate conditions, researchers suggest Corythosaurus was a selective feeder that ate the juiciest fruits and youngest leaves.
facts.quote: Based on the climate of the Late Cretaceous, they guessed that Corythosaurus would have been a selective feeder, eating only the juiciest fruits and youngest leaves.

facts.statement: A preserved Corythosaurus specimen contained conifer needles, seeds, twigs, and fruits in its chest cavity, implying it was a browser that fed on various plant parts.
facts.quote: A Corythosaurus specimen has been preserved with its last meal in its chest cavity. Inside the cavity were remains of conifer needles, seeds, twigs, and fruits, meaning that Corythosaurus probably fed on all of these, implying that it was a browser.

facts.statement: The complex internal structures of the Corythosaurus crest likely allowed it to produce calls used for warning or attracting mates.
facts.quote: The internal structures of the crest of Corythosaurus are quite complex, making possible a call that could be used as a warning or for attracting a mate.

facts.statement: Scientists speculate that Corythosaurus could produce loud, low-pitched cries similar to a wind or brass instrument, like a trombone.
facts.quote: Scientists speculate that Corythosaurus could make loud, low pitched cries "like a wind or brass instrument", such as a trombone.

facts.statement: Corythosaurus emitted low-frequency sounds through its nasal passages when it exhaled.
facts.quote: The nasal passages emit low-frequency sounds when Corythosaurus exhaled.

facts.statement: Despite variations in nasal passage ranges among lambeosaurines, they likely all produced low-pitched sounds.
facts.quote: However, even though the range for different lambeosaurine nasal passages vary greatly, they all probably made low-pitched sounds.

facts.statement: It is debated whether crested hadrosaurs like Corythosaurus were aquatic; early theories based on mistaken webbing have been disproven, showing the structures were actually padding.
facts.quote: When they were first described, crested hadrosaurs were thought to be aquatic, an assessment based incorrectly on webbing that is now known to be padding.

facts.statement: It has been proven that the Corythosaurus crest had no holes and that water pressure at 3 meters would prevent lung inflation, refuting the theory that it used the crest for breathing while diving.
facts.quote: However, it has now been proven that the crest did not have any holes in the end and the water pressure at even 3 m would be too great for the lungs to be able to inflate.

facts.statement: Both juvenile and adult Corythosaurus possessed a premaxilla-nasal fontanelle.
facts.quote: Juvenile Corythosaurus, along with adults, had a premaxilla-nasal fontanelle.

facts.statement: Young and adult Corythosaurus have sinuous skull sutures, distinguishing them from Parasaurolophus, while resembling Lambeosaurus and Hypacrosaurus.
facts.quote: Young and adult Corythosaurus are similar to Lambeosaurus and Hypacrosaurus, but dissimilar to Parasaurolophus in that the sutures of the skull are sinuous, not smooth and straight.

facts.statement: Over fifty articulated specimens from many different genera have been found in the Dinosaur Park Formation.
facts.quote: In the Dinosaur Park Formation, over fifty articulated specimens have been found that come from many different genera.

facts.statement: Earlier studies recognized four genera and thirteen species in the Dinosaur Park Formation area based on differences in size and crest shape.
facts.quote: Earlier, four genera and thirteen species were recognized from the formation's area when paleontologists used differences in size and crest shape to differentiate taxa.

facts.statement: Comparisons with modern reptiles suggest Corythosaurus may have been cathemeral, active throughout the day at short intervals.
facts.quote: Comparisons between the scleral rings of Corythosaurus and modern reptiles suggest that it may have been cathemeral, meaning it was most active throughout the day at short intervals.

facts.statement: The presence of a thin stapes and large eardrum implies Corythosaurus had a sensitive middle ear.
facts.quote: The presence of a thin stapes (an ear bone that is rod-like in reptiles), combined with a large eardrum, implies the existence of a sensitive middle ear.

facts.statement: Originally, Brown classified Corythosaurus as a member of the family Trachodontidae, which is now known as Hadrosauridae.
facts.quote: Originally, Brown referred to Corythosaurus as a member of the family Trachodontidae (now Hadrosauridae).

facts.statement: Brown classified Corythosaurus in the subfamily Saurolophinae, separating it from other genera like Hadrosaurus and Trachodon which were placed in Trachodontinae.
facts.quote: Brown classified Hadrosaurus, Trachodon, Claosaurus, and Kritosaurus in Trachodontinae, whereas he classified Corythosaurus, Stephanosaurus, and Saurolophus in Saurolophinae.

facts.statement: Brown later revised the phylogeny of Corythosaurus, finding it closely related and possibly ancestral to Hypacrosaurus.
facts.quote: Later, Brown revised the phylogeny of Corythosaurus, finding that it was closely related and possibly ancestral to Hypacrosaurus.

facts.statement: A 2014 study published in PLOS ONE identified Corythosaurus as the most derived lambeosaurine and the sister taxon to Hypacrosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2014, a study including the description of Zhanghenglong was published in the journal PLOS ONE. The study included an almost complete cladogram of hadrosauroid relationships, including Corythosaurus as the most derived lambeosaurine and being the sister taxon to Hypacrosaurus.

facts.statement: Corythosaurus shares similar-looking skulls and crests with other hadrosaurs like Hypacrosaurus and Lambeosaurus, except for Olorotitan.
facts.quote: With the exception of Olorotitan, they all share similar looking skulls and crests.

facts.statement: Research published in 2003 suggests that Olorotitan, despite having a unique crest, is Corythosaurus's closest known relative.
facts.quote: However, research published in 2003 has suggested that even though it possesses a unique crest, Olorotitan is Corythosaurus's closest known relative.

facts.statement: Corythosaurus lived from approximately 77 to 75.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Corythosaurus lived from ~77–75.7 million years ago.

facts.statement: In the Oldman Formation, the only Corythosaurus species present, C. casuarius, lived from about 77 to 76.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: In the Oldman Formation, C. casuarius, the only species of Corythosaurus from the deposits, lived about 77 to 76.5 mya.

facts.statement: In the Dinosaur Park Formation, C. casuarius lived from 76.6 to 75.9 million years ago, while C. intermedius lived from 75.8 to 75.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: In the Dinosaur Park Formation, C. casuarius lived from 76.6 to 75.9 mya, with C. intermedius living from 75.8 to 75.7 mya.

facts.statement: Corythosaurus likely lived in woodland forests and may have occasionally wandered into swampy areas.
facts.quote: Corythosaurus probably lived in a woodland forest and might have occasionally wandered into swampy areas.

facts.statement: Corythosaurus is known from many complete specimens, including a nearly complete holotype discovered by Barnum Brown in 1911.
facts.quote: Corythosaurus se conoce de muchos especímenes completos, incluido el holotipo casi completo encontrado por Barnum Brown en 1911.

facts.statement: Corythosaurus is known for many skulls with high crests that resemble those of a cassowary or a Corinthian helmet.
facts.quote: Corythosaurus es conocido por muchos cráneos con altas crestas. Las crestas se asemejan a las crestas del casuario o a un casco corintio.

facts.statement: The most probable function of the crest is vocalization, where sound waves would travel through many chambers and amplify when the animal exhaled, similar to a trombone.
facts.quote: La función más probable de la cresta es la vocalización. Como en un trombón, las ondas de sonido viajarían a través de muchas cámaras en la cresta, y luego se amplificarían cuando el Corythosaurus exhalara.

facts.statement: A Corythosaurus specimen was preserved with its last meal in its thoracic cavity, containing conifer needles, seeds, branches, and fruits.
facts.quote: Un espécimen de Corythosaurus se ha conservado con su última comida en su cavidad torácica. Dentro de la cavidad había restos de agujas de coníferas, semillas, ramas y frutos.

facts.statement: Corythosaurus has an estimated length of 9 meters, and its skull, including the crest, measures 70.8 centimeters in height.
facts.quote: Corythosaurus tiene una longitud estimada de 9 metros, y tiene un cráneo, incluida la cresta, que mide 70,8 centímetros de alto.

facts.statement: The genus Corythosaurus was named by Brown in 1914.

facts.statement: Corythosaurus intermedius was described by Parks in 1923 as a subdivision of the genus.
facts.quote: subdivision: Corythosaurus intermedius Parks, 1923

facts.statement: Synonyms for Corythosaurus include Corythosaurus excavatus (Gilmore, 1923), Stephanosaurus intermedius (Parks, 1923), Procheneosaurus erectofrons (Parks, 1931), Tetragonosaurus erectofrons (Parks, 1931), Corythosaurus bicristatus (Parks, 1935), and Corythosaurus brevicristatus (Parks, 1935).

facts.statement: Studies suggest that Corythosaurus and other coexisting dinosaurs occupied slightly different ecological niches to avoid direct competition for food.
facts.quote: Studies of the jaw anatomy and mechanics of these dinosaurs suggests they probably all occupied slightly different ecological niches in order to avoid direct competition for food in such a crowded eco-space.

facts.statement: Corythosaurus likely fed on conifer needles, seeds, branches, and fruits found in its stomach contents.
facts.quote: Corythosaurus probablemente se alimentó de todos estos elementos.

facts.statement: Benson and colleagues estimated in 2012 that the average length of Corythosaurus was 9 meters.
facts.quote: Benson et al. en 2012 estimaron que Corythosaurus tiene una longitud promedio de 9 metros.

facts.statement: A previous length estimate by Richard Swann Lull, published in 1942, found a total length of 9.4 meters.

facts.statement: In 1962, Edwin H. Colbert used specific dinosaur models, including Corythosaurus, to calculate its weight.
facts.quote: En 1962, Edwin H. Colbert usó modelos de dinosaurios específicos, incluido Corythosaurus, para calcular su peso.

facts.statement: The Corythosaurus model used was created by Vincent Fusco for a mounted skeleton and supervised by Barnum Brown.
facts.quote: El modelo de Corythosaurus utilizado, fue modelado por Vincent Fusco parade un esqueleto montado, y supervisado por Barnum Brown.

facts.statement: After testing, it was concluded that the average weight of Corythosaurus was 3.82 tons.
facts.quote: Después de la prueba, se concluyó que el peso promedio de Corythosaurus fue de 3.82 toneladas.

facts.statement: Recent size estimates published in 2001 found that the genus Corythosaurus is among the largest hadrosaurs.
facts.quote: Estimaciones de tallas más recientes de Corythosaurus, publicadas en 2001, encuentran que el género está entre los hadrosáuridos más grandes

facts.statement: The total length of the Corythosaurus specimen AMNH 5240 was 8.1 meters, with a weight of 3.0785 tons.
facts.quote: La longitud total del espécimen de Corythosaurus AMNH 5240 fue de 8.1 metros, con un peso de 3,0785 toneladas.

facts.statement: More than 20 skulls of this dinosaur have been found.
facts.quote: Más de 20 cráneos se han encontrado de este dinosaurio.

facts.statement: Corythosaurus was a herbivore that exhibited gregarious behavior and fed on low plants and forest fruits.
facts.quote: Corythosaurus era un herbívoro que presentaba un comportamiento gregario y se alimentaban de plantas bajas y frutos de los bosques.

facts.statement: Its beak had no teeth, but the jaw had hundreds of small ones that were constantly replaced as they fell out.
facts.quote: Su pico no tenía dientes, pero sí la mandíbula, en la que había cientos de pequeños y eran reemplazados constantemente a medida que caían.

facts.statement: Like other lambeosaurines, this animal had a high, elaborate bony crest on its skull containing elongated nasal passages.
facts.quote: Como con otros lambeosáuridos, este animal tenía una cresta ósea alta, elaborada encima de su cráneo, que contenía canales nasales alargados.

facts.statement: Scientists speculate that Corythosaurus could make a sound "like low howls like the wind or a brass instrument."
facts.quote: Los científicos especulan que Corythosaurus podría hacer un sonido "como gritos graves como el un viento o un instrumento de latón".

facts.statement: When herds of different genera mixed, its crest, which possibly served to attract females, and its keen sense of smell likely helped it return to its own group.
facts.quote: Cuando manadas de diferentes géneros se mezclaban, su cresta, que posiblemente debe haber servido para atraer hembras y su agudo sentido olfativo debe haberle ayudado a retornar con los suyos.

facts.statement: It was once thought that this dinosaur lived mostly in water due to the appearance of its webbed hands and feet.
facts.quote: Alguna vez se pensó que este dinosaurio vivió sobre todo en el agua, debido al aspecto de manos y de pies palmeados.

facts.statement: However, it was later discovered that the supposed "membranes" were actually pads of fatty tissue, as found in many modern mammals.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, fue descubierto más adelante que las supuestas "membranas" era de hecho almohadillas de tejido liposo, como se encuentran en muchos mamíferos modernos.

facts.statement: A set of characters was indicated by Barnum Brown in 1914 to distinguish Corythosaurus from all other Alberta hadrosaurs.
facts.quote: Un conjunto de caracteres fue indicado por Barnum Brown en 1914 para distinguir a Corythosaurus de todos los demás hadrosáuridos de Alberta

facts.statement: In 1916, in the revised version, Brown expanded the set of characters to include more features.

facts.statement: The supposed snout traits are incorrect because Brown confused the premaxillae with nasal bones and nasal bones with frontals.
facts.quote: Los supuestos rasgos del hocico son incorrectos porque Brown confundió los premaxilares con los huesos nasales y los huesos nasales con los frontales.
